summary: This task's own worktree/branch contains no code changes at all -- the diff is a 12-insertion/71-deletion rewrite of PROGRESS.md only. Per PROGRESS.md's own account, the worker located PR #53's actual head branch (worker/task-20260727-122935-projexa-e2e--pm-site-engineer-role-model, confirmed via `gh pr view 53`), checked out a separate task's worktree, and committed+pushed the real fix (commit 77de705) there instead of in this task's own isolated branch. That violates the dispatch model's own-worktree/own-branch rule and the no-scope-collision guarantee it exists to provide: two independently dispatched tasks (this one, and task-20260727-122935) are now entangled on one branch with no clear record of which task's audit trail owns the commit, and a third, apparently-duplicate task (worker/task-20260727-130236-fix-pr-53-audit-findings--punch-list-pat, same title, zero commits) sits alongside it -- evidence the pre-dispatch duplicate-scope check was not applied. Having gone and read the actual code on the foreign branch (commit 77de705) to do a real review: the two claimed fixes are substantively sound -- the punch-list PATCH route now carries a requireRole(ROLE_GROUPS.FIELD) gate identical to its sibling POST, and the new PATCH /api/org-members/[id] role-assignment endpoint is correctly gated to ROLE_GROUPS.ORG_ADMIN (owner/admin), validates the incoming role against ALL_ORG_ROLES, and is covered by reasonable unit tests for both routes. One real gap survives: the new role-assignment endpoint has no guard against demoting/removing an org's last owner/admin, which could strand an org with zero ORG_ADMIN-eligible users and no in-product recovery path -- the same class of lockout risk this change was written to close, just relocated and untested. Given tier2 always requires human sign-off regardless of verdict, and given the branch-ownership ambiguity this task created needs to be resolved (confirm which task legitimately owns commit 77de705, and reconcile/close the duplicate task-20260727-130236) before this can be treated as this task's completed, mergeable output, this is rejected as submitted -- not because the underlying security fix is wrong, but because this task did not produce a reviewable, isolated artifact of its own and instead mutated another task's branch out-of-scope.
issues: This task's own diff is documentation-only (PROGRESS.md rewrite); the actual code fix (commit 77de705) was committed and pushed directly to a different, independently-dispatched task's branch (worker/task-20260727-122935-projexa-e2e--pm-site-engineer-role-model, which is PR #53's real head branch per `gh pr view 53`), violating the isolated-worktree/own-branch rule in SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md and leaving ownership of that commit ambiguous between two tasks.

A likely-duplicate task branch exists with the same title/objective and zero commits (worker/task-20260727-130236-fix-pr-53-audit-findings--punch-list-pat), indicating the required pre-assignment duplicate-scope check was not applied before this task was dispatched.

On the actual fix reviewed on the foreign branch: PATCH /api/org-members/[id] has no guard preventing an org's last owner/admin from being demoted or reassigned, which could lock the org out of every ORG_ADMIN-gated route (including this recovery endpoint itself) with no in-product recovery path -- untested and unaddressed.

Minor/non-blocking: ROLE_GROUPS.ORG_ADMIN grants 'admin' the ability to promote any member (including itself) to 'owner' via this endpoint; verified this is not a real privilege escalation since 'owner' and 'admin' are treated identically everywhere else in the codebase (grep confirmed no other special-cased 'owner' check), but it is a naming/UX inconsistency worth a follow-up note.
